The '''2019 Munster Senior Hurling Championship final''' was a [[hurling]] match that was played on 30 June at the [[Gaelic Grounds]] in [[Limerick]]. It was contested by [[Tipperary county hurling team|Tipperary]] and [[Limerick county hurling team|Limerick]].<ref>{{cite web|url= https://www.irishtimes.com/sport/gaelic-games/hurling/tipperary-and-limerick-to-meet-again-in-final-1.3927329|title =Tipperary and Limerick to meet again in final|date=16 June 2019|work=Irish Times|accessdate=20 June 2019}}</ref>
Limerick won the game on a 2-26 to 2-14 scoreline to win their 20th Munster title.<ref>{{cite web|url= https://www.rte.ie/sport/gaa/2019/0630/1059309-tipperary-v-limerick-munster-final-updates/|title =Recap: Limerick 2-26 Tipperary 2-14|date=1 July 2019|work=RTE Sport|accessdate=3 July 2019}}</ref>	
 		
==Build-Up==
Tickets for the final went on sale on 19 June and ranged in price from €35 to €40 in the stand and €25 to €30 in the terrace. Terrace tickets sold out on the first day.<ref>{{cite web|url= https://www.independent.ie/sport/gaelic-games/hurling/limerick-and-tipp-munster-final-set-to-be-a-sellout-38236392.html|title =Limerick and Tipp Munster final set to be a sell-out|date=20 June 2019|work=Irish Independent|accessdate=20 June 2019}}</ref>			
<ref>{{cite web|url= https://www.rte.ie/sport/gaa/2019/0618/1056093-gaa-say-provincial-final-pricing-is-fine/|title = GAA satisfied with pricing for provincial final tickets|date=19 June 2019|work=RTE Sport|accessdate=19 June 2019}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url= https://www.limerickleader.ie/news/sport/424424/no-public-sale-of-stand-tickets-for-limerick-v-tipperary-hurling-final-confirmed-by-munster-gaa.html|title =Limerick v Tipperary hurling final confirmed by Munster GAA|date=19 June 2019|work=Limerick Leader|accessdate=19 June 2019}}</ref>

The final was the first final between the sides at the [[Gaelic Grounds]] since [[1996 Munster Senior Hurling Championship final|1996]], which ended in a draw before Limerick won the replay in [[Páirc Uí Chaoimh]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://munster.gaa.ie/history/sh_teams/|title=Munster Final Winning Teams|work=Munster.gaa.ie|accessdate=23 June 2011|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20110721124423/http://munster.gaa.ie/history/sh_teams/|archivedate=21 July 2011|url-status=dead}}</ref>

Before the senior final, the [[2019 All-Ireland Minor Hurling Championship|Munster minor hurling final]] between Limerick and [[Clare GAA|Clare]] took place at 11.30am, with Limerick winning the game by 1-17 to 1-11.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.the42.ie/limerick-munster-minor-hurling-clare-4703792-Jun2019/ |title =O'Neill hits 0-9 as Limerick defeat Clare to claim first Munster hurling title of the day|date=1 July 2019|work=The 42|accessdate=5 July 2019}}</ref>	
 						
The match was televised live on RTÉ2 as part of ''[[The Sunday Game]]'', presented by [[Joanne Cantwell]], with analysis by [[Anthony Daly (hurler)|Anthony Daly]], [[Donal Óg Cusack]] and [[Henry Shefflin]]. Commentary on the game was provided by [[Ger Canning]] alongside [[Michael Duignan (hurler)|Michael Duignan]].{{fact|date=October 2021}}

==Match==
===Summary===
Playing with the wind in the first half, [[Séamus Callanan]] scored a goal for Tipperary in the 18th minute when he ran in on goal after a pass from Noel McGrath to shoot low to the left corner of the net, this put Tipperary into a 1-6 to 0-4 lead. [[Peter Casey (hurler)|Peter Casey]] got a goal for Limerick in the 26th minute, flicking to the net after a pass from the left by [[Aaron Gillane]].<ref>{{cite web|url= https://www.irishtimes.com/sport/gaelic-games/hurling/limerick-send-out-imperious-statement-of-intent-as-tipperary-filleted-1.3942193|title =Limerick send out imperious statement of intent as Tipperary filleted|date=1 July 2019|work=Irish Times|accessdate=5 July 2019}}</ref>	
Limerick had a 1-11 to 1-9 lead at half-time. Tipperary's second goal came from [[John McGrath (Tipperary hurler)|John McGrath]] in the 44th minute when he got free to shoot to the right of the net. [[Kyle Hayes]] got a second goal for Limerick in the 55th minute running in on goal to flick to the net to put them six points in front.<ref>{{cite web|url= https://www.the42.ie/munster-hurling-final-live-scores-4703733-Jun2019/|title =As it happened: Limerick 2-26 Tipperary 2-12|date=1 July 2019|work=The 42|accessdate=5 July 2019}}</ref>
